candidate.answerReason: Fifteen full recipes are needed for 216 cookies. They use 45 tablespoons of butter, so six 8-tablespoon sticks are necessary and sufficient.

methods.label: Count full pans, then full sticks
methods.explanation:
First find how many full recipes are needed, because the butter must cover those complete recipes. Fourteen pans make \(14\cdot15=210\) cookies, which is too few. Fifteen pans make \(225\) cookies, so they need \(15\) recipes.

Each recipe uses \(3\) tablespoons of butter, giving a total of
\[
15\cdot3=45\text{ tablespoons}.
\]
Five sticks supply only \(5\cdot8=40\) tablespoons, while six supply \(6\cdot8=48\). Therefore they need \(\boxed{6}\) sticks of butter, choice \(\text{B}\).
methods.levelReason: Both whole-number decisions are justified by elementary multiplication and comparison.

candidate.annotationRationale: The task requires choosing the least sufficient whole number twice: first for recipes and then for butter sticks. This is the elementary ceiling meaning. Per-pan yield, butter per recipe, and tablespoons per stick are supporting quantitative relationships.
